prompt: Locked-off static camera on a tripod, fixed frame, no camera movement at all: one continuous unbroken shot from the first frame. A silent horror film from 1919, black and white, heavy film grain, gentle projector flicker, dust and scratches, the gas lamp's pool of light on the bench. [00:00-00:01] Stillness. The man in the top hat sits motionless, smiling straight into the lens, mouth closed, eyes fixed on us. [00:01-00:02] Without looking away from us, his gloved right hand, the one nearest the other person, makes one slow, lazy flick of the fingers towards the soldier, a bored brush-off, then drops back to rest. His smiling face stays frozen like a mask, perfectly still. [00:02-00:05] The soldier plants his crutch on the ground and slowly hauls himself up onto his one leg, the pinned trouser below the knee hanging empty. Leaning on the crutch, he limps away to the right, out of the lamplight, and is swallowed by the darkness at the edge of frame. [00:05-00:06] The man has not moved: same closed-mouth smile, same unblinking stare into the lens, the empty half of the bench beside him. Silence, only the faint hiss of the gas lamp. The camera stays completely still for the whole shot, one single take. Thanks.
